sections.h2: Which way of selling suits a Venice owner who needs speed?
sections.html:
Venice owners can sell for cash, list on the open market or find a buyer on their own. Flood exposure often decides which one works, because elevation and repair history shape what buyers and insurers will accept.

  • Cash buyer: fewer conditions and a closing date you choose, at a price that absorbs the buyer's risk.
  • Listing: more eyes and often a higher number, at the cost of prep work and patience.
  • Storm-damaged house: expect questions about permits, invoices and any flood claim on file, whichever route you take.

Your route also affects how soon the buyer's insurance quote arrives, and on an older coastal house a slow quote can hold up a closing. Venice sits on the Gulf side of Sarasota County. Its planned downtown, restored 1927 train depot and fishing pier give buyers a sense of where a house stands in the city's layers: older streets near downtown, newer annexations toward the interstate. Say which one yours belongs to when you write the listing or pitch a cash buyer.

Storm history now comes up in almost every conversation about a Venice house. Hurricane Ian in 2022 did more than $10 million in damage in the city. Hurricanes Helene and Milton in 2024 flooded the Golden Beach neighborhood and destroyed the South Jetty.

Water or wind damage raises three questions from any buyer: what was repaired, by whom, and whether the permits closed. A complete folder shortens negotiation.

  • Invoices and contractor names for every repair.
  • Permit records showing each one closed.
  • Dated photos from before and after the work.
  • Insurer letters and any flood claim history.

The Sarasota County Property Appraiser's website links a Hurricane Evacuation Levels reference. Look up the level for your address and mention it in your listing notes, since out-of-town buyers often ask about it before they ask about price. A house left unrepaired can still sell. Describe its condition honestly, and expect an offer that reflects the work left to do.

Venice limits repair spending in flood hazard areas. Once restoration or renovation costs reach half of the structure's pre-damage market value, with labor counted, the rule applies and the work must meet current flood standards.

The Florida Building Code adds a foot of freeboard above base flood elevation to reach design flood elevation. Anything built below that level, such as a garage or enclosure, cannot be living space. The owner signs a non-conversion agreement before a Certificate of Occupancy issues, and Sarasota County Public Records holds the recorded copy for later buyers.

Call the Building Division before repairs to learn whether the lot is in a Special Flood Hazard Area and how the city values the structure. The division also wants a call before any change to grade, and reports of unpermitted work.

Sarasota County charges the usual state stamp rate on the deed, and the clerk takes it along with recording fees at filing. Everyone on the deed shares liability. Ask the title agent for a combined total before accepting an offer, since a mortgage that stays on the house counts toward the price.

Owners can also join the Clerk's free fraud alert, an email notice whenever a deed or mortgage is recorded under a registered name. A seasonal resident selling from out of state benefits most.

sections.h2: Property taxes after a Venice sale
sections.html:
The seller's exemption ends at closing. The buyer's value is reset the next January 1, so the capped growth the seller enjoyed (2.7 percent for 2026 on the state chart) goes away. Plan on a buyer's bill that looks different from yours.

Tax bills go out each fall, and owners can enroll with the collector to get future bills by email. A Florida constitutional amendment on homestead taxes helps both sides to understand what is coming: the 2026 bill must be paid as issued, voter-approved changes first reach the 2027 bill, and school taxes plus non-ad valorem charges such as fire protection and solid waste remain on the notice.

Planning to buy again in Florida? Phone the appraiser at 941.861.8200 about moving part of your savings to the next home, a claim with a March 1 deadline.

Both situations run on court clocks, so talk to a Florida attorney early. A foreclosure sale follows judgment within a window set by statute. Heirs of a Venice house may qualify for a shortened probate route, depending on the size and age of the estate. The state's estate tax does not apply to deaths after 2004.

If you want to choose your own buyer instead of leaving the outcome to a court, a private sale before the auction date is the way to do it. A title company can show what liens, if any, must be paid from the proceeds.

For an inherited house, collect the death certificate, the will if there is one and any insurance policy on the property. Whoever has legal authority to sell, usually the personal representative, must sign the deed. Without that authority, no buyer's title company will close, so settle that question first.

sections.h2: How a Venice sale moves from offer to closing
sections.html:
Most quick sales follow the same path, and each stage has a Venice twist.

  1. You gather permits, invoices and any flood or insurance letters.
  2. A buyer makes an offer, usually after walking the house and checking its flood zone.
  3. The title agent searches the record for liens and for the recorded non-conversion agreement, if the house has one.
  4. The agent prepares a settlement statement showing deed tax, recording fees and your share of the tax bill.
  5. You sign the deed, and the clerk records it.

A buyer who needs a mortgage or a new insurance policy adds time at the third and fourth steps. A cash buyer can often skip both, which is why cash closings on coastal houses finish sooner when the paperwork is in order.

sections.h2: Who issues permits for work on a Venice house?
sections.html: The city's Building Division handles permits, flood questions and reports of unpermitted work, and its number is (941) 486-2626. Check for open permits before you list. An unclosed permit on a house with storm repairs is one of the most common reasons a buyer asks for a lower price or a delay.

faqs.q: Can I sell a storm-damaged Venice house without repairing it?
faqs.a: Yes. Cash buyers purchase houses as they stand and price in the repairs. Keep permits, photos and insurer letters, and ask the Building Division whether the 50 percent rule might apply.

faqs.q: What is a non-conversion agreement in Venice?
faqs.a: It is a document in which the owner promises that space below design flood elevation, such as a garage, will not become living area. The city requires it before a Certificate of Occupancy and files it with county records.

faqs.q: How much is the state deed tax on a Venice sale?
faqs.a: Seventy cents per $100 of price, the rate everywhere but Miami-Dade. The clerk collects it at recording and every party to the deed is liable.

faqs.q: Does my homestead exemption pass to a Venice buyer?
faqs.a: No. It ends with the sale, and the buyer's value resets on the next January 1. You may carry part of your capped savings to a new Florida home through portability.

faqs.q: Who should I call about permits?
faqs.a: The city's Building Division at (941) 486-2626. Ask about open permits before you list, and report any unpermitted work there.
